report.finding: The model and parameters are fine. The session integrator is set to `gillespie` (stochastic SSA), not the deterministic CVODE integrator, so every call to `simulate()` produces a different sample trajectory by design — that's exactly what "20, then 22, then 25" is. There is no uninitialised state or numerical bug; the apparent non-reproducibility is the expected behaviour of a stochastic simulator with a free-running RNG.
report.evidence:
`rr.getIntegrator()` shows `name: gillespie`. Running `rr.reset(); rr.simulate(0,20,200)` twice in a row gives different final [S1] values (15 vs 20) even though species/parameters are reset each time. Setting `rr.integrator.setValue('seed', 12345)` immediately before each `reset()+simulate()` call instead gives identical results both times ([20,14] and [20,14]), confirming the variability is purely the stochastic RNG advancing between calls, not garbage state.

If deterministic ODE output was actually wanted, switching to `rr.setIntegrator('cvode')` reproduces the same trajectory every time trivially, since there's no randomness at all.

recommended_changes.why: Re-set this seed value immediately before each simulate() call (after rr.reset()) to get reproducible Gillespie trajectories; leaving it fixed once at the start is not enough since the RNG state advances across calls. Alternatively switch to the deterministic 'cvode' integrator if stochasticity was not intended.
